intentions.title: Give scaffolded Barkpark Next.js apps a complete, working marketing site out of the box (not a bare hello-world)
intentions.evidence: layout.tsx defines a full header/nav/skip-link/footer shell; about, pricing, contact, and posts/[slug] pages are real content-backed pages, not stubs — running `create-barkpark-app` yields a deployable multi-page site.

intentions.title: Every content page is driven live from Barkpark documents, so editing content in Studio updates the site with zero code changes
intentions.evidence: about/page.tsx, pricing/page.tsx, posts/[slug]/page.tsx all call getDoc/getDocBySlug from '../../lib/barkpark' and render via @barkpark/react PortableText; each falls back to a friendly 'Run pnpm seed' message when the doc is missing rather than crashing.

intentions.title: SEO metadata (title, description, OpenGraph, canonical) is derived automatically from Barkpark document content on every page
intentions.evidence: generateMetadata() in about, pricing, and posts/[slug] pages calls barkparkMetadata(page, ...) from @barkpark/nextjs; layout.tsx sets metadataBase from NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL so relative OG/canonical URLs resolve correctly in prod vs localhost.

intentions.title: Editing content in Barkpark Studio propagates to the live Next.js site via webhook-driven revalidation, without manual redeploys
intentions.evidence: api/barkpark/webhook/route.ts wires createWebhookHandler + revalidateBarkpark from @barkpark/nextjs/webhook and /revalidate, force-dynamic + nodejs runtime, secret-gated via BARKPARK_WEBHOOK_SECRET; comment documents Studio-side webhook config.

intentions.title: The starter demonstrates the full write path — visitor-submitted forms create Barkpark documents through Server Actions
intentions.evidence: contact/page.tsx is a client component using useActionState + submitContact server action (contact/actions.ts) that 'creates contact documents via the Barkpark mutate API' per its own copy, with accessible aria-live status feedback.

intentions.title: The scaffolded site meets baseline accessibility and production hygiene (WCAG skip-links, live regions, robots/sitemap, error/loading/not-found boundaries) without extra developer effort
intentions.evidence: layout.tsx includes a WCAG 2.4.1 skip-to-content link and dark-mode-aware focus styles; contact form uses role=status aria-live=polite explained via inline comment; robots.ts, sitemap.ts, error.tsx, loading.tsx, not-found.tsx are all present as standard Next.js App Router conventions shipped by default.
